The Problem For France

Charles Gave

Gavekal Research | 6 Oct 2026

As the spreads on French government debt blew out last Thursday, my colleague in Gavekal’s Paris office, Cedric Gemehl, asked “How Wide Can French Spreads Get?” I have nothing to add to his conclusions about the specifically French part of the problem. But I am very interested in the broader underlying malady, of which France’s current complaint is today’s most visible symptom.I have been arguing for some time that the world has entered a period of structurally rising real interest rates. The story starts with the stock of excess savings built up by Asia following the 1997-98 crisis. The accumulation of these excess savings led to a big decline in real rates all over the world.
